title: F. Love at Cafe Liebe (Easy Version)

legend: This is the easy version of the problem. The problems differ in their constraints and input formats. A solution to one may not work for the other.

Kanako-chan loves Hime-chan secretly, so she wants to give her as much coffee as possible (Hime is a caffeine addict). There are n%%ZSMJ0%% types of coffee numbered from 1%%ZSMJ1%% to n%%ZSMJ2%%, but Hime is only interested in type 1%%ZSMJ3%%.

Kanako was offered help by Sumika-senpai. Sumika has an unlimited supply of certain types of coffee. Specifically, you are given a binary string s%%ZSMJ4%% of length n%%ZSMJ5%%, where si=1%%ZSMJ6%% if and only if Sumika has coffee of type i%%ZSMJ7%%. Kanako can ask for any non-negative real amount of coffee of each type that Sumika has, as long as the total volume of coffee she requests is at most v%%ZSMJ8%%.

After getting some coffee from Sumika, Kanako can then trade with other customers at Cafe Liebe. In particular, there are m%%ZSMJ9%% customers willing to trade. To trade with the i%%ZSMJ10%%-th customer, Kanako must do the following:
Choose a non-negative real number k%%ZSMJ11%%.
Give the customer kai%%ZSMJ12%% cups of coffee xi%%ZSMJ13%% and kbi%%ZSMJ14%% cups of coffee yi%%ZSMJ15%%.
In return, the customer will give Kanako kci%%ZSMJ16%% cups of coffee zi%%ZSMJ17%%.
Kanako can trade with customers as many times as she wants. What is the maximum amount of coffee of type 1%%ZSMJ18%% she can obtain?
input: Input consists of multiple tests. The first line contains t%%ZSMJ19%%, the number of tests (1≤t≤50%%ZSMJ20%%).

The first line of each test contains n%%ZSMJ21%%, m%%ZSMJ22%%, and v%%ZSMJ23%%  — the number of coffee types, the number of customers, and the maximum amount of starting coffee (1≤n≤50%%ZSMJ24%%, 0≤m≤103%%ZSMJ25%%, 1≤v≤1018%%ZSMJ26%%).
The second line contains a string s%%ZSMJ27%% of length n%%ZSMJ28%% consisting of 0s and 1s. The i%%ZSMJ29%%-th character is 1 if and only if Sumika has coffee of type i%%ZSMJ30%%.

The next m%%ZSMJ31%% lines contain 6%%ZSMJ32%% integers each: ai%%ZSMJ33%%, xi%%ZSMJ34%%, bi%%ZSMJ35%%, yi%%ZSMJ36%%, ci%%ZSMJ37%%, and zi%%ZSMJ38%%, describing their trades (1≤xi,yi,zi≤n%%ZSMJ39%%, 1≤ai,bi≤5%%ZSMJ40%%, ci=1%%ZSMJ41%%). It is guaranteed that xi%%ZSMJ42%%, yi%%ZSMJ43%%, and zi%%ZSMJ44%% are all distinct.
In the easy version, it always holds that ci=1%%ZSMJ45%%.
output: For each test, output a floating-point number, the answer.
Your answer is considered correct if its absolute or relative error does not exceed 10−6%%ZSMJ46%%.
Formally, let your answer be a%%ZSMJ47%%, and the jury's answer be b%%ZSMJ48%%. Your answer is accepted if and only if |a−b|max(1,|b|)≤10−6%%ZSMJ49%%.
note: In the first test, you can ask for 8%%ZSMJ50%% cups of type-2 coffee and 12%%ZSMJ51%% cups of type-3 coffee. Then, you trade with customer 1%%ZSMJ52%% using k=4%%ZSMJ53%%, and thus recieve 4%%ZSMJ54%% cups of type-1 coffee. We can show this is the maximum achievable.
In the second test, we cannot obtain any coffee of any type no matter what, so we output 0%%ZSMJ55%%.
